speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) how many and what proportion of workers at healthcare institutions are currently outsourced; (b) what proportion of outsourced workers perform roles which in the pre-outsourcing era would have been in frontline or patient care areas or involving handling patient samples; and (c) whether human resource practices for outsourced workers are harmonised with direct hires, including recognition for COVID-19 related work and frontline exposure risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In general, the third party contractors have been engaged by the public healthcare institutions under a contract for service arrangement for specific projects or services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: They are engaged for a fee and take on the responsibility of hiring the staff required to meet the needs of these projects or services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Hence, the compensation and benefits of staff that they hire is determined and paid by these contract companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The public healthcare institutions appreciate the contribution of these outsourced workers in our battle against COVID-19 and many of these institutions have extended goodwill donations and care packs to their outsourced staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Ministry certainly encourages the public healthcare institutions to continue looking into ways to show appreciation for the hard work of outsourced staff in many different ways.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have two supplementary questions I would like to put to MOH.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I ask this again, Mr Speaker, because in the pre-outsourcing era, these workers would have been in-sourced, would have been direct hires and in the pre-outsourcing era, they would have qualified for similar bonuses and support.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And it would also be in harmonisation with the existing measures the Senior Minister of State has mentioned – provisions of vaccination support and PPE support.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, I raise this for the Ministry's consideration, please.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And I am sure the healthcare institutions will look at ways to honour their hard work and sacrifices, and the risks that they take as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will give the healthcare institutions the latitude and the time to plan for appreciation in the various ways that they can to show solidarity with these workers who have also taken risks, just like any of our other healthcare workers in the frontline sector.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Ministry make it a requirement for service providers to extend work injury compensation to outsourced healthcare workers?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: It would be specific to the service providers, because these are outsourced workers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There are situations – not exactly in the healthcare setting but sometimes, other settings – where the worker is on a contract for service arrangement and no Work Injury Compensation Act or WICA benefits accrue to such workers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I am wondering whether healthcare institutions make it a requirement for companies that provide such outsourced services to healthcare institutions, whether it is a requirement by the healthcare institutions themselves for these workers to have WICA coverage.
